author: Codex
changed: Observe descendant termination within a bounded two-second signal-delivery grace period rather than assuming every OS schedules the killed descendant before the parent is reaped.
proves: Actual flood and deadline controls still require the owned process to exit or become a zombie; running descendants fail the check. This does not skip or weaken the group-kill requirement.
limits: A killed zombie is not a running worker. Remaining Linux, current-source and protected publication checks are pending; no new scope closure or tag accuracy claim.
